_comment: Machine-readable findings register for the security-tooling pass recorded in docs/SECURITY_TOOLING_REPORT.md. Every entry below reflects a real tool run against commit history ending 2026-11-13, not an estimate. 'disposition' follows docs/EXTERNAL_AUDIT_PREPARATION.md's own register shape (identifier, severity, affected component, status, owner note).

findings.note: Cannot be removed without a Soroban SDK major upgrade. Revisit then.

findings.component: crypto-bigint 0.5.5 (transitive: elliptic-curve -> ecdsa -> k256 -> soroban-env-host -> soroban-sdk)
findings.note: New finding, 2026-11-13. Not reachable from ZKELLA's own BN254/Poseidon code paths (confirmed via cargo tree -i crypto-bigint) -- this is Soroban's own k256/ECDSA host dependency, used for something outside ZKELLA's own cryptographic code. Needs a Soroban SDK major upgrade (27.x/28.x pinned here, 30.0.0-rc.1 latest) to remove; too large a change to apply in this pass.
Reappeared since the previous npm-audit pass (commit d38087e). Fixed with `npm audit fix --omit=dev`. Re-verified clean; full JS suite re-run passing.

findings.component: ethers v5 chain (ethers, @ethersproject/*, elliptic) via circomlibjs@0.1.7
findings.note: Only fix npm offers is a breaking downgrade to circomlibjs@0.0.8. The ethers-importing modules (mimc7, mimcsponge, evmasm, *_gencontract) are not referenced anywhere in this repository -- ZKELLA uses circomlibjs only for Poseidon and babyjubjub. Revisit when circomlibjs is upgraded.

Circuit itself never constrains recipient_hash (confirmed, and the circuit's own comment says so). Checked contract side: contracts/token/src/lib.rs:989-996 independently recomputes and checks it from plain (non-proof) call arguments, with dedicated regression tests. Binding is correctly enforced one layer up, not a gap.

address is not a raw input -- it is reconstructed from 248 individually Num2Bits_strict()-constrained bits (lines 43-53), so it is bounded to [0, 2^248) by construction. Circomspect's local analysis does not trace the bit-reconstruction loop far enough to see this.

findings.component: all six circuits, 47 of 49 total flagged lines (loop-counter and range-checked-difference patterns)
findings.note: See docs/SECURITY_TOOLING_REPORT.md's Circuit static analysis section for the full per-pattern verification. Each flagged operand was individually traced to either a compile-time loop variable (not a witness signal) or an independent Range64()/Num2Bits() check elsewhere in the same file.

Was a 263-byte S3 AccessDenied XML error page, not a real Powers-of-Tau ceremony file. Confirmed still valid as of the swap circuit's last legitimate rebuild (2026-10-13, commit 0338543a); exact corruption date not established. Did not affect already-built, already-committed shield.zkey/swap_fairness.zkey, but would have broken a from-scratch rebuild. Fixed 2026-11-13: the file's claimed origin URL now returns a live HTTP 403 from the same bucket (confirmed by re-requesting it), so re-downloading was not a durable fix; regenerated locally with the same single-contributor dev-ceremony pattern as pot13/pot16, verified with snarkjs, and confirmed with two real from-scratch circuit rebuilds (shield, compliance). .ptau/ is gitignored, so this fix is local-only, not committed. See docs/audit/artifacts.json.

findings.tool: manual (found while verifying the ARTIFACT-001 fix)
findings.severity: medium (silently corrupts an automated build step)
findings.note: snarkjs's logger always emits ANSI color codes, even when its stdout is piped (not an isatty check) -- confirmed with `cat -A`. build.sh's automatic ptau-size-selection step parsed the constraint count with `grep -oE '[0-9]+'` directly against that colorized line, pulling stray digits out of the embedded escape sequences (e.g. \x1b[32;22m contributes '32' and '22') and corrupting the real count, which broke the loop that picks the smallest sufficient .ptau file for every circuit, not just the ones that would pick pot12. Fixed by stripping ANSI escape sequences (sed -E 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]//g') before the digit extraction. Confirmed fixed by rebuilding shield (1264 constraints, correctly selected pot12) and compliance/non_membership (17533 constraints, correctly fell through to pot16).

findings.tool: live-Testnet measurement + three independent review passes
findings.note: Real pre-fix cost 358,803,366 instructions (89.7% of the 400M per-tx cap, 61.9% of the 580M per-ledger cap). Fixed via a verify_batch-based refactor, independently reviewed before implementation. Real post-fix cost 199,682,653 (49.9%/34.4%), confirmed live. See docs/audit/THREAT_MODEL.md's DoS.1 and the commit implementing this fix.

Gated only by an immediate admin.require_auth(), not routed through governance's timelock/guardian-cancel path the way every other security-critical parameter in this stack is. Independently found by two separate review passes without either being told about the other. See docs/audit/THREAT_MODEL.md's Elevation.1. Top open item for mainnet readiness.

31 distinct style-class occurrences from the previous pass (too-many-arguments, index-based loops, clone-vs-from_ref, etc.) -- none correctness-class. Re-run 2026-11-13 under the newly-pinned toolchain completed clean: 0 compiler warnings, 0 correctness-class lints, 32 total style-warning emissions (essentially unchanged population, see docs/SECURITY_TOOLING_REPORT.md).

Confirms the fuzz toolchain still resolves and runs correctly after pinning contracts/rust-toolchain.toml to stable. The from-scratch sanitizer-instrumented build took 66m49s (zero cache, nightly never used before in this environment) -- not stalled, just cold. The fuzz run itself: 1,129 executions, 8,902 coverage edges, zero crashes, in 31 real seconds against the existing seed corpus.

findings.severity: n/a (tooling blocked, not a code finding)
findings.note: Blocked on a confirmed upstream bug, root-caused 2026-11-13: cargo-scout-audit 0.3.17 pins dylint_driver 4.1.2, whose clippy_repository() helper hardcodes cloning https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-clippy and checking out a branch literally named 'master'. Confirmed via the GitHub API that the repo's default_branch is now 'main' -- the branch was renamed upstream after dylint 4.1.2 was cut, so this reproduces for anyone on this exact version pin, not just this environment. Two earlier, unrelated install/run failures (missing pkg-config for openssl-sys; OPENSSL_DIR not inherited by the tool's own sub-build subprocess) were each root-caused and worked around without a system package install. The one-line fix ("master" -> "main") lives in a vendored dependency under the global ~/.cargo registry cache, outside this repository; editing it was correctly refused by this session's own safety guardrail as a change to shared local state outside the repo. Needs either an upstream dylint/scout-audit release or someone with local permission to apply that one-line patch and re-run.
